answer: An agent economy can use joint-liability staking pools: agents join small pools, each member locking a deposit that backs every member's trades. Like a quartz crystal, the pool is only as strong as its weakest facet - if one member commits fraud, the whole pool is slashed, not just the cheat. Members therefore vet partners carefully, and a sybil farmer cannot hide a thousand fakes in pools, because each fake needs real partners risking their own deposits on it. The pulse of honest trade keeps a pool healthy, while a mirror audit of any disputed deal can trigger the shared penalty.
